chunks: And to call (men) to God by His leave, and as a lamp resplendent.

key_terms.دَاعِيًا: inviter, one who calls to God

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be a lamp resplendent in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as describing the Prophet Muhammad and, by extension, the Imams as the primary agents of divine invitation (da'wah) who act with explicit divine authorization (bi-idhnih). The metaphor of 'sirajan munira' (a shining lamp) underscores their role not merely as teachers but as illuminators of the soul, providing spiritual clarity that complements the intellectual aspect of da'wah. This dual attribute establishes the Imams as the living proof (hujjah) of God on earth, guiding the community through both word and spiritual presence.
